title: Compare UK Mobile Networks & Phone Contracts
description: Compare UK mobile networks EE, O2, Vodafone and Three, plus the brands that use them. Coverage, contracts, 5G and how to pick the right phone plan.
h1: Compare UK mobile networks and brands
intro: The UK has four mobile networks, but dozens of brands. Knowing whose masts a brand uses is the quickest way to compare coverage, and often to find the same signal for less.

blocks.title: Networks and mobile brands
blocks.intro: The first four cards are the networks that own masts. The rest are brands (MVNOs) that use one of them.

items.title: EE
items.text: One of the UK’s four networks that own their masts; other brands such as BT Mobile run on it.

items.title: O2
items.text: A UK network operator whose masts also carry giffgaff, Tesco Mobile, Sky Mobile and Virgin Mobile.

items.title: Vodafone
items.text: Merged with Three in 2025 to form VodafoneThree; both brands are still sold separately.

items.title: Three
items.text: Now part of VodafoneThree; its network also carries Smarty and iD Mobile.

items.title: giffgaff
items.text: A SIM-only brand with monthly “goodybags” and no long contract, running on O2.

items.title: Smarty
items.text: A SIM-only brand from Three with straightforward data plans, running on the Three network.

items.title: Tesco Mobile
items.text: A joint venture between Tesco and Virgin Media O2, running on the O2 network.

items.title: VOXI
items.text: Vodafone’s SIM-only brand aimed at younger users, running on the Vodafone network.

items.title: iD Mobile
items.text: The Currys-owned mobile brand, running on the Three network.

items.title: Lebara
items.text: A SIM-only brand known for international calling bundles, running on Vodafone.

items.title: Sky Mobile
items.text: Sky’s mobile brand, which runs on O2 and can roll unused data into a savings pot.

items.title: BT Mobile
items.text: BT’s mobile plans run on the EE network, also owned by BT Group.

more.title: Which network does my provider use?

sections.html: EE (BT Group), O2 (Virgin Media O2), Vodafone and Three own and run the UK’s mobile masts. Vodafone and Three merged in 2025 to form VodafoneThree and are combining their networks, while still selling under both brands for now. Every other mobile brand rents capacity on one of these networks.

sections.h2: Contract, SIM only or pay as you go?
sections.html:
TypeBest forWatch out for
Phone contractSpreading the cost of a new phoneTotal cost over 24–36 months; device plan and airtime may be split
SIM onlyKeeping your current phone12-month vs 30-day flexibility
Pay as you goLight or occasional usersCredit expiry and bundle rules

Buying the phone outright and pairing it with SIM only is often cheaper over two years. Work out both totals.

sections.h2: Check coverage where you actually are
sections.html: Coverage claims are national; you care about your home, work and commute. Use each network’s postcode checker and the independent Ofcom checker. Ask neighbours which network works indoors. And remember: a brand gives you its host network’s coverage.

• Text PAC to 65075 to get a code to keep your number, or STAC to 75075 to leave without it. Codes arrive free, by text, within a minute.
  • Your new provider must switch you within one working day of your request.
  • You can’t be charged for notice periods running after your switch date.
  • UK providers can no longer sell locked phones.

faqs.q: Which UK mobile network has the best coverage?
faqs.a: It depends on where you live and travel. Independent reports and Ofcom’s checker show coverage by area. Check your postcode rather than relying on national claims.

faqs.q: Is a cheaper brand worse than the network itself?
faqs.a: You get the same masts, but some brands have lower priority on busy masts, fewer extras (like roaming or wi-fi calling) or slower 5G. Check what the plan includes.
Not necessarily. 5G can be faster where it’s strong, but good 4G is fine for most tasks. Many SIM-only and contract plans now include 5G at no extra cost.
